transcript_header:
Date: 2026-03-03 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Gomez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Reynolds (Aurora InfoSec), Jon Park (Aurora Procurement), Liam O'Neill (Aurora Cloud)
summary: Walkthrough of Aurora's SIG/CAIQ questionnaire focusing on SOC 2 docs, SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit logs / log retention, data residency, and KMS integration. Redwood clarified hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options; agreed to share SOC 2 report and RBAC screenshots. Action items assigned for evidence exchange and follow-up call next week.
topics: Audit logs and retention / SIEM integration
transcript: [00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me are Elena and Priya from our security/SE team. How are you all?
[00:08] Maya: Hi Samir, thanks. Maya here. We have Jon and Liam on as well. Looking forward to walking through the SIG, we flagged a few high priority controls.
[00:18] Jon: Yep, procurement side - we'll need documentation and timelines for legal review, mainly focus on SOC 2 and evidence exportability.

[00:27] Elena: Great. Our plan is to go section by section of the SIG, call out where we have standard evidence and where we may need to collect screenshots or run exports for you. Quick note: sometimes the auto-transcript will show 'SOC two' instead of SOC 2 haha.
[00:40] Liam: Totally fine. Our primary concerns: data residency for EU customers, key management (KMS/HSM), and audit logs to feed into our SIEM. Also SSO and RBAC so we can limit access per team.

[00:52] Samir: Understood. We'll cover each. To start: SOC2 and ISO. We are SOC 2 Type II for our hosted control plane, and we have an ISO 27001 cert in progress - expected later this year. I'll drop the SOC 2 report and scope in the follow up.
[01:10] Maya: When you say 'hosted control plane' do you mean Redwood-hosted? We operate in a regulated line of business and prefer not to send sensitive PII outside our VPC.

[01:20] Priya: Good question. Redwood supports three modes: hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For regulated workloads we recommend Private — customer-managed networking, optional onprem package, and KMS integrations. There's also an intermediate 'Dedicated' which is single-tenant GPU pools but still managed and may meet some compliance needs.
[01:45] Liam: For data residency, can we choose EU-only regions for Private?

[01:49] Elena: Yes, Private lets you pin region and use your own cloud tenancy in most cases. We also provide options for KMS—bring-your-own-key via KMS/HSM integrations so keys never leave your control. We'll share architecture diagrams.

[02:05] Jon: On audit logs - we need immutable logs for all user activity and model inference requests, retention for 2 years, and the ability to stream to our Splunk instance. Can Redwood support that?

[02:16] Priya: We produce detailed audit logs: authentication events, role changes, API request traces (not raw model outputs by default to avoid PII), and admin actions. For Private/Dedicated we can forward logs to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder and set retention policies. For hosted we have export APIs and longer term retention add-ons.
[02:38] Maya: Regarding SSO: we use SAML with SCIM provisioning. Does Redwood support SCIM for group sync and enforced MFA on sign-in?

[02:47] Elena: Yes, SSO via SAML is supported across both hosted and private, SCIM provisioning for groups is supported in Dedicated and Private now; hosted has similar capabilities but provisioning model depends on tenancy. MFA enforcement is supported via SSO provider; we integrate with IdP policies. We'll include sample SAML configs.
[03:05] Liam: Any nuance around RBAC? We want least privilege by default, ability to assign model-level permissions and restrict access to embeddings or log download. How granular is RBAC?

[03:15] Priya: Our RBAC supports role templates and custom roles. You can scope permissions by project, model, and route. For Private deployments you can also enforce network policies. We'll export sample policy JSON and screenshots of the RBAC UI.
[03:33] Jon: On encryption: are model inputs encrypted at rest, and is there envelope encryption with customer keys?

[03:40] Elena: At-rest encryption is standard; for Private/Dedicated we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via KMS. For hosted you can request a dedicated tenant and BYOK in some plans. We'll note where evidence is available.
[03:52] Maya: About the SIG spreadsheet itself, some answers we may want to modify — when you say 'we have a process' we need to provide the process doc. Do you typically append evidence links?

[04:00] Samir: Yes, standard practice: we answer the SIG/CAIQ items in the spreadsheet and attach evidence links (PDFs/screenshots/log extracts). We'll share the completed spreadsheet and a zip with the artifacts. If any control requires a special attestation we'll note that.
[04:15] Liam: Example: for the control around network segmentation — we need VPC peering details and network ACLs. Can you give a sample network diagram?

[04:23] Elena: We'll include an architecture diagram for Private showing VPC peering, subnets, and NAT/GW flow. For Dedicated we show how the single-tenant GPU pools sit in their own VPC with restricted egress.
[04:40] [05:00] Samir: Quick check — anyone on the call has specific legal clauses in the vendor terms we need to be aware of? SLA, data processing addendum?
[05:06] Jon: We'll review the DPA; our legal team typically requests standard DPA plus audit rights. We may ask for an on-site audit for Private but we'll confirm.
[05:15] Priya: Audit rights are usually covered in enterprise contracts; for Private it's easier to arrange audit access because you're in your own tenancy. We'll flag the legal team for next steps.
[05:26] Maya: On logging detail, can we get sample audit log entries? We need to prove immutability and show who triggered a model invocation plus tokenized request IDs.

[05:36] Elena: Yes, we'll export an anonymized sample log set, masking any PII. It shows timestamp, user id, action, resource, and request id – and we can demonstrate the append-only storage with retention policies.
[05:50] Liam: How about model artifacts — do you store model weights or do they get pulled dynamically? There's concern about model provenance and if our private models will be isolated.

[05:59] Priya: For hosted we host weights; for Private you can bring your own model artifacts in your storage or have them deployed into your VPC. Model provenance is part of our onboarding checklist; we can provide a chain-of-custody doc for custom models.

[06:12] [06:40] Samir: Moving to specific SIG sections: authentication and identity management — question A1 about centralized identity. Answer is yes, we integrate with major IdPs via SAML/OIDC, and we support SCIM for group sync. Evidence: SAML metadata, SCIM config examples, MFA enforcement policy.
[06:35] Maya: We'll need those config examples. Also can Redwood support conditional access policies from the IdP? For example, block login outside corporate IP ranges.
[06:43] Elena: Conditional access is enforced at the IdP; we respect the assertions. For Private, you can also restrict access at the network level and enforce client IP allowances.
[06:56] Jon: Question on data retention — what is the retention for request logs by default on hosted and can we increase it?

[07:05] Priya: Hosted default is 90 days for detailed request logs, with longer aggregated metrics retained for a year; retention add-ons are available up to multi-year retention for audit logs. Dedicated/Private you control retention via config and your storage choices.
[07:22] Maya: Is the content of prompts stored in logs? We need to avoid storing PII.

[07:28] Elena: By default we avoid storing full user content in long-term logs; request metadata and redacted traces are kept, and there's an option to disable content logging entirely. For Private you can set your ingestion to drop content or send to your own storage.
[07:43] Liam: For SIEM integration, do you support pushing via Kafka or syslog?
[07:48] Priya: We support syslog, S3 exports for batched pulls, and Kafka/webhook integrations for near-real-time forwarding. We'll document endpoints and example configs.

[07:59] [08:20] Samir: Quick aside, sometimes transcript text shows product names odd—like 'Redwood Private' gets turned to 'Redwood Privet' in some auto transcripts, so don't worry if you see weird typos later.
[08:31] Maya: (laughs) good to know. Next: encryption in transit — TLS versions and cipher suites?
[08:36] Elena: We require TLS1.2+ for client connections and prefer TLS1.3. We can provide a security spec with ciphers and TLS policies for your infosec review.
[08:47] Jon: For KMS, do you integrate with AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault, HSM vendors?

[08:52] Priya: Yes — BYOK via AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault supported; we also have HSM integrations for customers requiring FIPS-level key storage. We'll include the KMS integration guide and the HSM vendor list.
[09:05] Liam: Is there support for rotating keys automatically?

[09:09] Elena: Key rotation can be scheduled via customer KMS. We don't rotate customer-managed keys automatically without your consent; we support rotation best practices and will show proofs of rotation events in the audit log when configured.
[09:23] Jon: On backup and disaster recovery — what are RTO/RPO commitments for Dedicated vs Private?

[09:30] Priya: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and typical RTOs measured in minutes for compute reallocation; Private RTO depends on your self-managed infra but we provide runbooks and recommended architectures. We'll include our SLA doc and typical RTO/RPO figures.
[09:46] Maya: Any pen test reports we can review?

[09:51] Samir: We have third-party pentest reports for the platform; some are shared under NDA — we'll provide the latest redacted executive summary and the pen test vendor report under an NDA if needed.
[10:03] Liam: For the SIG control about vulnerability management, do you have a cadence for patching and CVE handling?

[10:09] Elena: Yes, we run continuous scanning and have a documented CVE response process; average time to patch high severity is within our published SLAs — we'll include the policy and a recent CVE response example.

[10:22] [10:50] Jon: Regarding procurement timelines, once we get the SIG and the SOC2 report we typically have a two-week legal review; if Private is selected procurement may take longer. We'll aim to conclude vendor assessment by end of March.
[10:58] Samir: Sounds good. We'll prioritize the SOC2 and the SIG export. Elena will collect RBAC screenshots and sample logs. Priya will compile the KMS and network architecture docs.
[11:12] Maya: A couple of specific SIG items — CAIQ question A2 about privileged access: who are your privileged admins and how is access to production limited?

[11:22] Priya: Privileged admin list is limited, MFA required, and access is logged via our IAM; for Private you can map your own admin roles. Evidence will be admin list, access review policy, and screenshot of role attestation logs.
[11:36] Liam: For data in transit to model runtime — is there any caching or third-party CDN that could break data residency?

[11:44] Elena: No third-party CDN for request payloads. We have internal caching for KV cache to optimize latency but for Private you control cache placement and policies. We'll document cache behavior and how to disable cross-region caching.
[11:58] Jon: Does Redwood redact or tokenize PII automatically in logs?
[12:02] Priya: We have optional PII redaction pipelines; if you're concerned we recommend ingest pipelines that mask or hash identifiers before storage, and we can show an example.
[12:12] Maya: On legal side, we may request subprocessor list — can you provide that?
[12:17] Samir: Yes, standard subprocessor list will be included; we'll also flag partners who handle telemetry or analytics.

[12:26] [12:50] Elena: Quick note on model fallbacks: our runtime supports graceful degradation — if a preferred model isn't available we can route to a compatible variant; this is important for availability but customers can opt out if they want strict determinism.
[12:41] Liam: Is there an audit trail for model rollouts and who triggered them?
[12:46] Priya: Yes, rollouts are logged with actor, timestamp, and model version. We'll include rollout audit examples.
[12:58] Jon: If we need a technical deep dive on performance and KV cache behavior we may schedule a separate session with your infra team.
[13:05] Samir: Happy to set that up — we can run a small benchmark in a Private sandbox if you want. We'll note that as an optional next step.
[13:14] Maya: Two items: 1) We'll need SOC2 and SIG ASAP, 2) we need to know if you can support EU data residency for all logs and artifacts.

[13:21] Elena: For EU residency: yes for Private, for hosted we have EU regions and data residency options but some artifacts like billing may remain in US — we'll call out any exceptions in the evidence pack.
[13:35] [14:00] Samir: Anything else from procurement/legal?
[14:06] Jon: We might request a demo of the admin console and RBAC before final sign-off. Also pricing question for Dedicated vs Private — will give to procurement separately.
[14:16] Samir: We'll send a dedicated pricing sheet but legal and security docs first. Action items recap at the end.
[14:25] Maya: Regarding evidence for incident response — we need your IR plan and SLA for notification timelines on incidents affecting our data.

[14:34] Priya: We have an incident response policy with 72-hour notification for reportable incidents; for high-severity incidents we notify immediately and follow up with a timeline. We'll include an IR playbook excerpt.
[14:46] Liam: Can you also show how alerts are emitted to our ops channel? We want webhook or pager integration.
[14:53] Elena: We'll include webhook examples and alerting integrations with PagerDuty and Opsgenie.
[15:02] Jon: For retention of audit logs at 2 years, is there any cost estimate?
[15:07] Samir: Yes there is a retention add-on cost; I'll include ballpark numbers in the follow-up pricing attachment.
[15:16] [15:45] Maya: On the SIG question about backups we need to see your backup schedule and restore test results.
[15:24] Priya: We'll provide the backup schedule doc and a recent restore test report for the Dedicated environment.
[15:36] Jon: Also, please indicate which controls require additional attestation or custom contract language; that speeds legal review.
[15:42] Elena: We'll flag any non-standard items in the SIG answers and call them out as 'requires customer attestation' or 'requires custom contract clause'.

[15:53] Samir: Ok heads-up: we'll share the completed SIG spreadsheet by EOD Thursday and drop the SOC2 link; Elena will include RBAC screenshots and sample logs; Priya will add KMS/HSM docs and network diagram. Any timing conflicts?
[16:07] Maya: Thursday EOD works. We'll schedule the follow-up the week after — tentative March 10th at 15:30 UTC.
[16:17] Jon: Fine. We'll also prepare a short list of legal questions to send over in parallel.
[16:25] Liam: One last technical ask — can you confirm whether payload encryption keys are rotated per-request or per-session?

[16:31] Elena: Key rotation is per KMS policy; typically per-customer key rotation is periodic (months) but you can rotate session keys per invocation if you build that into your client. We'll include details.

[16:42] [17:10] Samir: Recap and next steps: 1) Share SIG export + SOC2 (Samir) 2) RBAC screenshots + sample audit logs (Elena) 3) KMS and network diagrams (Priya) 4) Customer to confirm residency regions and stakeholder list (Maya/Liam/Jon). We'll set tentative follow-up 2026-03-10.
[17:28] Maya: Thanks everyone — appreciate the thoroughness. We'll review artifacts internally and come back with any clarifying questions.
[17:36] Jon: Thanks, talk soon.
[17:40] Samir: Thanks all, closing now.
[52:00] <call ended>
